claim: The GC subsystem is the only component authorized to delete content-addressed objects.
GC must not delete an object while any session pin or committed reference names it, preserving `INV_NO_LOSS` and `INV_NO_DANGLE`.
GC runs as a background lease-holder loop and its safety does not depend on leadership uniqueness; concurrent or stale leaders may duplicate work but must not mis-delete.
Content blobs use keys of the form `blobs/<aa>/<blob_hash>` and are deduplicated across tables, while part manifests are immutable root-local objects with at most one structural owner.
A follower may steal the GC lease only after observing the incumbent `(owner, seq)` unchanged across the observation window and seeing no advancing heartbeat pulse.
The advisory GC heartbeat is stored in `gc/hb` as `{owner, hb_seq}` and is advanced independently of round progress to prevent a live slow leader from being falsely stolen.
If `gc/hb` is absent or belongs to a different owner, the lease protocol falls back to observing `gc/state.seq`.
The authoritative pool-wide GC shard count is persisted in generation-8 `_pool_meta`; `gc/state.gc_shards` mirrors it after GC state exists.

The current retired-in-snapshot refactor replaces the prose's three-cursor merge and separate `retired_refs` runs with a two-cursor source-edge merge, `kCondemned` sentinel rows, and a fold-seal `condemned_summary`.
GC discovery enumerates the live root-shard universe with `LIST(cas/refs/)`, and this LIST sweep is the only universe-proportional operation in a regular round.
Before discovery, `computeHeartbeatFloor` fences out expired writer mounts so their last commits are durable before the LIST sweep.
Heartbeat classification uses `live`, `terminated`, and `expired`; an expired non-terminated mount is fenced with a token-guarded overwrite that preserves its body and sets `gc_fenced`.
Fence-out settles liveness only; a fenced member's watermark, precommits, staging debris, roots, and mount slot remain until deliberate operator decommission.
The deliberate member-removal command is `SYSTEM CONTENT ADDRESSED DROP POOL MEMBER '<server_id>' FROM DISK '<disk>'`, with CLI equivalent `clickhouse-disks ca-drop-member`.
A GC fold processes only the root-shard journal window `(folded_cursor, current_shard_version]`.

A `new_binding` event contributes `+1` for each manifest blob, a true `old_binding` removal contributes `−1`, an equal old/new binding contributes zero, and a repoint contributes `−1` for the old manifest plus `+1` for the new manifest.
GC must not advance a fold cursor past a live precommit whose manifest body is absent or fails `RefMatchesBody` or `ManifestNamespaceMatches` validation.
A missing precommit body is non-activating; when the body appears, the fold activates it and emits its `+1` deltas, while an abandoned precommit emits no deltas.
Attempt-scoped GC artifacts are written under `gc/gen/<G_f>/attempt/<a>/` before adoption, and an unadopted attempt is invisible to readers.
Deterministic GC artifacts such as in-degree runs and fold seals must be byte-identical on collision, otherwise GC fails with `CORRUPTED_DATA`.
The single `gc/state` CAS atomically publishes the adopted generation and attempt, folded cursors, retired references, round, and prune cursor.

A crash before the round CAS leaves the prior generation authoritative; the next pass reruns from a fresh attempt and previously issued exact-token deletes are idempotent through `NotFound` or `TokenMismatch`.
Snapshot-run consumers use streaming reads with fixed linear-scan requests of `head`, tail `get`, and forward-only `getStream`, retaining only the footer index and one block.
Reading every run block with a separate ranged GET was rejected because a full 8 GB run would require about 32,000 requests per shard.
`getStream` is permitted only for write-once objects such as runs and seals; mutable objects remain on `get`.
When a GC-shard delta bucket is empty, the fold carries the parent generation's `RunRef` without run I/O; zero run I/O requires both the delta bucket and retired state to be empty.
The persisted in-degree authority is the set of active source edges identified by `(ManifestId, path)`, with edge IDs computed by `sourceEdgeId(ManifestId, path)`.
Source-edge activation is set union and removal is set difference, so refolding either operation is idempotent.
`in_degree(blob)` is computed as the cardinality of its active source-edge set during a round and is not persisted as a separate counter.
Persisting integer refcounts and folding `prior_count + Σ ±1` was rejected because a refolded removal can underflow the count and wedge GC with `CORRUPTED_DATA`.
Only blobs with an explicit zero-transition marker in the current generation are GC candidates; a blob never observed as a reference target is not a candidate.
Any clamp anomaly sets `suppress_destructive` for the pass, preventing graduation and pending or exact-token deletes until a clamp-free pass.
If a blob is already absent at condemnation time, GC records no candidate and never fabricates a delete token from a 404.
A retired entry whose in-degree recovers above zero is spared even when it is already `delete_pending`.
GC's writer freshness marker is a per-hash `.meta` object with `Clean` and `Condemned` states; a writer that reads `Condemned` aborts reuse and re-uploads from source.
Physical deletion is two-phase: a floor-eligible entry is first published as `delete_pending`, and `deleteExact` runs only for an entry pending in the previous published list.
`deleteExact(blobKey, token)` treats `Deleted`, `TokenMismatch`, and `NotFound` as successful terminal outcomes for the corresponding delete attempt.
If an exact delete reports `created_delete_marker = true`, GC throws `LOGICAL_ERROR` because versioning tombstones can violate `INV_NO_RETURN`.
Part manifests are deleted only after the adopted fold has sealed their blob decrements, and pre-precommit debris is handled by a bounded exact-token orphan sweep.
Lazy journal trim compacts a shard when trimmable events reach `gc_trim_min_events` (default 256, with 0 meaning eager) or encoded body size reaches `gc_trim_body_soft_limit` (default 8 MiB).
B140-dangle was caused by separately durable snapshot edges and `folded_cursor`; embedding the cursor in the snap codec makes trim and snap coverage co-durable.
`PoolConfig::gc_snap_generations_to_keep` defaults to 3, and 0 disables generation retention pruning.
Generation pruning skips generations still referenced by the adopted seal, while a later parent-reference hand-off deletes the entire superseded generation prefix after the CAS.
A round uses `a = lease.seq` as its attempt identifier, so competing leaders write to distinct attempt prefixes and only the lease-token `gc/state` CAS can adopt one attempt.

The `gc_lock` in-process mutex was rejected because it blocked writers and limited GC to one process; exact-token deletion, attempt-scoped generations, and the lease provide split-brain safety instead.
Patch manifests are first-class reachability roots and keep both their own delta blobs and referenced base-part blobs alive while active.
A stateless reader without a `/parts` reference needs an ephemeral Keeper pin in the MARK union so its parts cannot be swept during a SELECT.
For a fixed namespace and shard, every recreated root shard has a strictly greater `incarnation`, and fold cursors are keyed by `(ns, shard, incarnation)`.

`dropNamespace` appends a tombstone as its last journal event, and GC may reclaim the shard object only after the tombstone and all prior journal events are folded; a token change from a revive prevents deletion.
A rebuild over trimmed journals fails closed with `CORRUPTED_DATA` when no healthy adopted baseline exists, rather than silently under-counting live edges.
A forced GC rebuild over-protects unowned manifests that are not provably build-dead, preferring bounded leaks over violating `INV_OVER_COUNT_ONLY` through under-counting.
GC ordering is biased toward over-counting: crashes may delay reclamation, but must never make GC under-count a live reference.
The ack-floor round reduces the example 100,000-table per-round request cost from about 2.4 million requests to about 2,000–3,000 plus the discovery LIST sweep.
Tests using the default `gc_shards=1` do not exercise sharded GC bugs; D1 fold and discovery tests must also run with `gc_shards > 1`.
A point-in-time `HEAD -> 404` is not durable absence; unreadable bodies clamp the fold and any clamped pass suppresses destructive decisions.

The three server-root control objects live under `gc/server-roots/<srid>/`: `owner` is a write-once identity anchor, `epoch` is a CAS-bumped monotone counter, and `mount` is a token-guarded lease body.
`server_root_id` must be non-empty, at most 255 bytes, contain no empty, `.` or `..` path segment, and not use reserved `_files` or `_manifests` segments; invalid IDs fail with `BAD_ARGUMENTS`.
The mount lease expiry is `expires_at_ms = now_ms + config.mount_lease_ttl_ms`, and the keeper renews at `config.mount_renew_period`.
The mount heartbeat's `min_active` field records the oldest in-flight `build_seq`, while `UINT64_MAX` is the farewell or retired sentinel.

GC fence-out of an expired lease and the Store's local write-fence are distinct mechanisms: GC persists `gc_fenced=true`, while Store latches local `lost` and gates ordinary ref mutations through `mayMutate()`.
A GC-fenced `(uuid, epoch)` mount cannot be refreshed in place; recovery must allocate a fresh writer epoch.
A same-UUID, same-epoch fenced mount yields `FencedSelf`, a foreign owner yields `ForeignOwner`, and a same-UUID live different epoch yields `LiveDoubleStart` from `claimMount`.
Read-only CA mode skips capability probing, watermark and mount claims, and GC; `fsck`, `ca-gc-dryrun`, `ca-gc-rebuild`, and `ca-inspect` require a read-only disk.
A hard-killed server's stale mount is waited out for at most the lease TTL plus margin before reclaim, while a live twin causes `LiveDoubleStart` and aborts.
When a running server detects that GC fenced its mount, it latches the local write fence, schedules remount, and retries with a fresh epoch without throwing from the remount loop.
A `Cas::Build` is never persisted and has no precommit replay path; GC never invents a ref transition or removes a dead precommit.
`runFsck` recomputes reachability from authoritative refs rather than GC snapshots and performs no writes.
`runFsck` labels `Reachable`, `Dangling`, `Unreachable`, `PendingGc`, `AwaitingGc`, `Unaccounted`, and `SnapshotOracleMismatch` objects, and `Unaccounted` is never used as a reachability input.
The SQL command `SYSTEM CONTENT ADDRESSED GC REBUILD [FORCE] [<disk>]` uses the same global `SYSTEM_CONTENT_ADDRESSED_GARBAGE_COLLECTION` access right as a regular GC command.
`clickhouse-disks ca-gc-rebuild [--force]` requires a read-only CA mount but writes exactly one `gc/state` CAS on success.
`FORCE` bypasses only the healthy-baseline refusal in `rebuildBaseline`; it does not bypass a competing leader or failed `gc/state` CAS.
`ca-gc-dryrun` requires read-only mode, calls `previewDeletes()` with fixed `Gc` ID `UInt128(1)`, and performs no writes.
Per-event CA audit logging is best-effort: a full SystemLog queue drops rows with a warning and never blocks the Core operation.
`system.content_addressed_mounts` reports one row per mount slot and classifies state as `live`, `expired`, `terminated`, `fenced`, or `corrupt`.
`CasGcIsLeader` is 1 while the local scheduler is leader, and `CasGcPendingReclaimEntries` reports the process-local reclaim backlog.

Six ProfileEvents—`ContentAddressedGenerationResurrectionsTotal`, `ContentAddressedDuplicateGenerationBytes`, `ContentAddressedTombstonesTotal`, `ContentAddressedGenerationsObserved`, `ContentAddressedHashesObserved`, and `ContentAddressedOrphanBytesEstimate`—have zero increment sites and describe a removed design.
`GC REBUILD` shares `SYSTEM_CONTENT_ADDRESSED_GARBAGE_COLLECTION` with regular GC, so the current access model cannot grant the two operations independently.
Mount events emitted inside `Store::open` are dropped because the CA event sink is installed only after open completes.
Invoking SQL `GC REBUILD` without a disk writes `gc/state` on every CA disk on the node, so requiring an explicit disk is a tracked safety/usability improvement.
In the current object model `ObjectKind` has only `Blob`; `Tree` and `CATR` were removed, while `PartManifest` is a protobuf body embedded in root-shard state.
Content-addressed immutable data uses binary encoding, mutable control and ref objects use protobuf, and the earlier JSON codec family was abandoned.
The normative protobuf package is `clickhouse.cas.format` in `cas_format.proto`, while the CMake target remains `clickhouse_cas_proto`.

The blob envelope has a fixed 256-byte header with a 94-byte core containing `magic`, `writer_version`, `compatibility_version`, `hash_algo`, `flags`, `header_len`, `logical_size`, `logical_hash`, `domain_id`, `incarnation_tag`, `build_id`, and `header_hash`.
The envelope core is never extended; new fields go into the `[94, header_len)` TLV area and `header_len` is padded to an 8-byte multiple with a pool payload offset of 256 bytes.
`compatibility_version > G_BUILD` decodes as `UNKNOWN_FORMAT_VERSION`, bad magic or header hash decodes as `CORRUPTED_DATA`, and unknown critical TLVs decode as `UNKNOWN_FORMAT_VERSION`.
The envelope's `domain_id`, `incarnation_tag`, and `build_id` are excluded from `logical_hash`, allowing a new physical incarnation without changing the content address.
The incarnation tag is carried in the object body rather than provider metadata so changing it creates a new backend token without a metadata copy and remains portable across S3, GCS, and Azure.
Blob identity is the streaming chunked hash of raw payload bytes using 2048-byte `DBMS_DEFAULT_HASHING_BLOCK_SIZE` blocks, not a one-shot hash of the whole payload.

`putDeterministicArtifact(Backend&, key, bytes)` is limited to GC-internal deterministic artifacts, and a pre-existing key is adopted only when its bytes are equal; divergent bytes cause `CORRUPTED_DATA`.
A blob hash covers `[header_len, EOF)` payload bytes and excludes the envelope header and incarnation zone.

Per-hash freshness metadata uses magic `CAMT` and two states: `Clean = 0` means referenceable body present, and `Condemned = 1` means GC marked zero in-degree while the body remains present for possible CAS resurrection.
Per-hash metadata is an advisory freshness point-read, not the blob lifetime linearization point; exactness remains with the in-body incarnation tag and exact-token body delete.
The standalone Merkle `treeId` design and `CasTreeCodec` are not implemented in the current code because the rev.15 `PartManifest` redesign replaced the standalone Tree object.
A separate intermediate tree-layer object was rejected because it added key-space and GC edge complexity without benefit beyond recursive subtrees and identity decoupling.

The physical CAS layout includes `blobs/<shard2>/<blobId>`, `cas/refs/<ns>/<shard_number>`, `cas/manifests/<ns>/<writer_epoch>/<build_seq>/<ordinal>.proto`, `gc/state`, `gc/hb`, `gc/gen/<gen>/attempt/<attempt>/`, and `gc/server-roots/<server_root_id>/{owner,epoch,mount}`.
`@cas@` is a suffix on a table-directory segment, never a standalone path segment; it marks the boundary between the mirrored ClickHouse path and the immutable CAS archive.
Atomic tables map to `store/<u3>/<uuid>@cas@`, while non-Atomic tables map to `data/<db>/<tbl>@cas@`.
No registered namespace may be a path-prefix of another namespace, because shard discovery uses prefix LIST and nesting would mix their keys.
Detached refs use the `detached/` prefix inside the table's own namespace rather than a sibling detached namespace.
A raw subtree deletion such as `rm roots/<server>/…` is destructive offline maintenance and is not equivalent to `dropNamespace`, because it bypasses the journal and fenced index pruning.
`Cas::Backend` exposes token-aware `get`, `getStream`, `head`, `putIfAbsent`, `putIfAbsentStream`, `putOverwrite`, `casPut`, `deleteExact`, and `list`, plus `supportsListTokens`.
Backend tokens must satisfy `head(k).token == prior get(k).token` only when the bytes are unchanged; this contract makes token-based decoded-shard caching safe.
`deleteExact(key, token)` removes only the matching incarnation and returns `TokenMismatch` without changing the object when the token differs.
`ObjectStorageBackend::get` converts a concurrent-delete `NoSuchKey` or 404 during GET into `std::nullopt`, matching `CasInMemoryBackend`.
`supportsListTokens()` is true only when LIST returns per-key incarnation tokens; without it GC must GET every root-shard body.
S3 and Azure use content-derived ETags as incarnation tokens, allowing CA to use the PUT response ETag without a follow-up HEAD; dedup reuse after `PreconditionFailed` still needs a HEAD.
GCS generation tokens are not content-derived, so generation stores disable LIST-token shortcuts and require the probed conditional dialect and token semantics.
GC discovery requires strong LIST consistency: an object PUT before the LIST boundary must appear in the discovery result.
The RustFS overwrite-leak workaround is a test-harness-only orphan reaper scoped to `roots/`; production CA code is unchanged.
Generation-1 format evolution uses `compatibility_version` write-down-to-floor: additive protobuf fields are skipped by old readers, while breaking binary changes require a floor-gated branch.
The durable roster and `max_content_addressable_pool_format` setting are designed but deferred as pre-release schema-evolution machinery.
`gc-snap` remains a versioned binary-plus-zstd GC-internal format rather than being converted to protobuf.
The current decommission feature is implemented without the durable roster through `SYSTEM CONTENT ADDRESSED DROP POOL MEMBER` and `ca-drop-member`; roster removal remains a future hook.
`REPLICATION_PROTOCOL_VERSION_WITH_CA_RELINK` is protocol version 10; mixed-version clusters negotiate the minimum version and automatically fall back to byte transfer.
The CA relink wire contract sends `pool_uuid` and encoded `PartManifest` bytes in the legacy `part_id` cookie as `part_manifest_v1`; sender identity fields in the body are non-authoritative.
A CA relink is advertised only for `try_zero_copy && !to_detached`, preventing byte-fetch fallback loops and ensuring detached fetches use the detached namespace.
Same-pool CA replication transfers a manifest instead of blob bytes; the receiver adopts shared-pool blobs into a fresh receiver-local manifest and publishes its own ref.
If CA manifest adoption fails because a referenced blob is missing or condemned, the receiver publishes nothing and retries the fetch with `try_zero_copy=false`.
A CA MergeTree part is modeled as many files to one manifest to one ref, so `freeze()` creates one whole-part `DiskTransaction` when the caller supplies none.
CA data-part reads consult in-flight transaction objects before committed metadata, providing read-your-writes for staged projection sub-parts.
The generic `ReadPipeline` FileView stage exposes a payload window `[left_bound, right_bound)` as a standalone file and translates downstream positions and right bounds by `left_bound`.

`ReadBufferFromFileView` must rebase position accounting from the implementation's real post-operation state and restore buffer swaps on exceptions; otherwise range reads can drift or retain swapped buffers.
`getResultObjectETag()` exposes the PUT or multipart-completion ETag after the upload finalize barrier so CA can record an incarnation token without a follow-up HEAD.

Native conditional copy uses `If-None-Match: *`; a 412 means the destination already exists and returns `{created=false}`, while disabling native copy fails with `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` instead of doing an unconditional copy.
Token-exact object deletion maps `If-Match` 412 to `TokenMismatch`, 404 to `NotFound`, and other errors to exceptions.
S3 412 responses are classified by `S3Exception::getExceptionName()` and are not retried; retrying unmodeled 412 errors caused a RustFS retry storm and long CA stalls.
Conditional requests with bodies at least `expect_continue_min_bytes` negotiate `Expect: 100-continue`; the default threshold is 1 MiB and the per-disk setting can lower it.
GCS conditional semantics require the native `GOOG4-HMAC-SHA256` dialect because GCS S3-compatible SigV4 silently ignores `If-None-Match` and `If-Match`.
GCS maps `If-None-Match: *` to `x-goog-if-generation-match: 0`, maps numeric `If-Match` to the corresponding generation condition, and rejects conditional multipart completion.
A generation-token store forces single-part conditional uploads and rejects versioned GCS buckets because exact-token delete would archive rather than reclaim the old generation.
The local object-storage test backend tolerates concurrent ref unlink during listing by treating vanished files as absent and using an explicit iterator stack.

The CA IO-layer extension points are CA-agnostic virtual interfaces with fail-closed defaults, while the MergeTree integration remains leaky through repeated `isContentAddressed()` branches and a seam header located inside the CA directory.
CA requires server-enforced conditional PUT, COPY, and DELETE semantics, a write-time incarnation token, bucket versioning off, and strong LIST consistency.
The user-facing integration settings added outside the CA directory are `expect_continue_min_bytes`, `http_client = gcs_hmac | gcp_oauth`, and the internal conditional-write knobs in `WriteSettings`.
CA tests write objects through the same production codecs used by readers, so the fixtures exercise real format round trips rather than white-box state pokes.
The default test fixture uses one root shard, `gc_trim_min_events=0`, and `gc_fold_max_defer_rounds=8`.

`CountingBackend` tracks per-key `head`, `get`, `getStream`, `put`, and `list` counts plus whole-read, ranged-length, and key-substring I/O metrics used to assert streaming-memory and idle-round behavior.

The test suite scripts concurrency hazards through backend subclasses and does not use sleeps to reproduce races; only `gtest_cas_part_folder_access.cpp` and `gtest_cas_ref_writer.cpp` use real `std::thread`.
`CasInstrumentedBackend` is an operation-counting ProfileEvents decorator, not a fault-injection backend.
The strongest whole-pool test oracle is `runFsck().dangling == 0` for no loss and `runFsck().unreachable == 0` after reclamation for no leak.

CA tests are single-process, single-threaded, and clock-free for GC scenarios; genuine concurrency correctness rests on backend primitives, TLA+ models, and integration or soak tests rather than gtests alone.
B140-dangle is pinned by tests requiring a shared deduplicated blob to survive dropping only one of two live refs.
B171 is protected by a durable build-root `+1` edge for adopted blobs and a fail-closed commit path that aborts when the dependency closure cannot be proven.
The S04/S04b under-count bug was fixed by replacing persisted integer in-degree with an idempotent source-edge set, making duplicate removals no-ops.
GC-WEDGE-2026-07-10 showed that an orphan sweep must preserve a dropped but unsealed committed manifest body until its removal decrement is folded.
RESURRECT-REUPLOAD-ORPHAN is prevented by tracking the `(hash, token)` incarnation so a replacement token starts a fresh condemnation cycle.
B151 requires a freshly written part's final ref to publish at lock-free tmp-to-final `moveDirectory`, with rollback dropping the early-published ref when the transaction is abandoned.
The CA praktika job runs the complete stateless suite with a CA disk as the default MergeTree storage, using local object storage and RustFS-backed S3 variants.
The RustFS CA stateless job is required because MinIO OSS lacks the enforced conditional deletes needed by the incarnation pool's fail-closed probe.
The integration test `test_cas_gc_sharded` exercises disjoint-shard GC with `gc_shards=2` and `blobShard = high64(hash) % 2`.

The `utils/ca-soak` harness uses a deterministic `splitmix64` seed to drive SQL workload and in-memory aggregate oracle, checks both replicas against the oracle, and finishes with `clickhouse-disks fsck`.
The base `CasSingleWriterSlot` renewal and foreign-touch failure paths have no gtest coverage and need a backend token-displacement test plus a crash-path test.
The background `CasGcScheduler` pacing loop and its error-swallow behavior have no dedicated gtest coverage.
Async-insert retry row loss from the dedup-token-versus-part hazard is documented but has no gtest; the soak defaults to `async_insert=0`.
The two disabled protocol scenario tests for subtree adoption are obsolete because the tree model was removed.
Unknown or future format versions are expected to raise `UNKNOWN_FORMAT_VERSION`; the test helper comment claiming `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` is stale.
B33's former Replicated-on-CA restriction is lifted; Replicated on a CA disk is now supported end-to-end.

`CaIncarnationCore.tla` proves `INV_NO_DANGLE`, `INV_NO_LOSS`, `INV_NO_RETURN`, and `INV_JOURNAL_COVERAGE` across adversarial writers, GC leaders, split-brain, resurrection, overwrite, and trimming scenarios.
The canonical incarnation model establishes exact-token deletion, fold-through-fence ordering, registry commit-time universe fencing, and evidence re-observation as load-bearing safety rules.
A writer publish gate must consult durable `deadTok[h]` as well as in-flight retired state; consulting only retired state can admit a physically dead token after deletion.
Any action that stops a token from being current must add the displaced token to `deadTok[h]`, and revalidation mode must check the current physical token in the same CAS.
A tree reference may be published only when all direct children are present and non-condemned at publish time.

`CaIncarnationCore.tla` is the architecture-independent safety spine, but its manifest-embedded journal and fence structure is superseded by ref-log objects, source-edge runs, fold seals, and heartbeat-floor fencing in shipped code.
The build-root model proves that both structural build-root reachability and fail-closed commit are necessary to prevent adopted-blob dangles; either half alone is insufficient.

The shipped writer uses lazy manifest-body edge discovery with a missing-body clamp barrier rather than the model's inline closure at precommit; this preserves the safety conclusion through a different mechanism.
`CaGcLeaseCore.tla` proves atomic lease-steal isolation and no false steal of an alive mid-round leader when the advisory heartbeat is enabled.
GC safety is independent of the advisory heartbeat; the heartbeat is the minimal addition needed to prevent a slow leader's frozen round sequence from triggering a false steal.

The mount model requires sticky server-root ownership, a durable monotone writer epoch, and observation-based reclaim over a stable holder token for a full TTL-plus-drift window on the reclaimer's monotonic clock.
Mount reclaim must not trust the foreign mount body's wall-clock timestamp and must install the successor's own mount body.
The per-write mount guard is a pure local check `!lost ∧ now < deadline`; superseded writers are blocked by the sticky local `lost` latch rather than a per-write shared-state read.
`CaB140DangleMerge.tla` proves that trim gating and storing the fold cursor with committed snap edges are jointly necessary and sufficient to prevent trim-before-durable dangles.

The incarnation registry-removal model proves that a durable per-shard never-reused incarnation and a newborn shard self-floor at the current GC round are both required; neither coordinate alone suffices.
The shard-incarnation model requires reclaim to wait until the shard journal, including its tombstone, is fully folded.
The writer-heartbeat `min_ack` half of `CaGcAckFloorCore.tla` is superseded by v3 freshness metadata, while its GC-round rebuild and clamp-suppression portions remain current.
The live GC-round graduation predicate is `condemn_round < current_round`, with `suppress_destructive` independently blocking graduation on a clamped pass.

`CaGcAckFloorZombie.tla` proves that two-phase `delete_pending` is required when two leaders interleave: a deposed leader may execute only deletes justified by pending state published before its pass.
The safety floor must be latched no later than the fold cut; reading it after the cut could graduate over a commit invisible to that pass's in-degree view.

`CaGcRootLocalPartManifestCore.tla` proves the root-local part-manifest invariants including no dangle, no loss, no return, journal coverage, single ownership, manifest-body validity, in-degree correspondence, and attempt-scoped visibility.

The root-local model shows that a target-sharded fold needs one global coordinator fence and paired old-binding `−1` deltas; per-reducer fencing or inferring the old target from the new ref is unsafe.
Only the adopted attempt's artifact may be consulted by GC decisions; a deposed leader's artifacts must remain reader-invisible.

The `SkipParksDeadPrecommit` model found that token-diff discovery could permanently park a static shard containing a watermark-dead abandoned precommit; the fix forces a read when the sealed coverage reports such a precommit.
A root ref may own at most one committed manifest; `Build::promote` must abort on a different existing committed manifest, while same-content republish is idempotent.
The resurrect-reupload orphan occurs when GC tracks a retired entry by hash only; settling the old token without re-condemning a replacement token can leave the replacement present forever.
The fix for resurrect-reupload orphan re-condemns the current token when a prior retired entry's token differs, and emits `blob_retire_replaced`.
`CaGcRoundDeferCore.tla` permits a non-destructive round to defer rebuilding the in-degree snapshot, but a due graduation must force-fold before deleting and deferral must be bounded.
The edge-before-observe model preserves the precommit → adopt/observe → promote order and K1 condemned-meta adoption gate; tokened leaves need no promote-time revalidation in the current code.
The current code trusts tokenless `adoptEvidence` leaves through durable manifest edges rather than performing the model's K3 presence HEAD and condemned check.

The raw immutable-body freshness-meta design with terminal tombstones was rejected because it introduced writer–GC waiting and liveness coupling; the current design keeps one hash key with an in-body incarnation tag and exact-token body deletion.
Per-incarnation blob keys such as `blobs/xx/<hash>.<incarnation>` were rejected because they require `404 → LIST` reads and propagate incarnation into manifests and parents.
The orphan sweep must skip a committed manifest body with a pending unsealed removal because the removal fold still needs the body to emit its decrement.
A clamped GC pass may hold back a landed reference, but must declare the clamp and suppress graduation and pending deletes until a later clamp-free pass consumes the held reference.
A disaster-recovery rebuild starts with an empty retired list, over-protects until the normal condemnation pipeline catches up, and mints its round above every surviving mount acknowledgement.
The original EBR/epoch GC model `CaGcCore.tla` was removed as superseded by the incarnation-token design.
